rookwood-database-markings.title: Markings

potterywheel-rookwood-marks.author: The Pottery Wheel

potterywheel-rookwood-marks.note: 1886: RP with no flames. 1887: one flame. 14 flames by 1900. Roman numerals below the mark after 1900 (XXII = 1922). Warns that the tail of the R looks like a flame. antique-marks-rookwood.author: antique-marks.com
antique-marks-rookwood.title: Collecting Rookwood Pottery & Dating Rookwood Marks

artpotteryblog-rookwood-marks.author: Art Pottery Blog
artpotteryblog-rookwood-marks.title: Rookwood Pottery Marks

entries.name: WEDGWOOD, impressed
entries.looks_like: The word WEDGWOOD in plain capitals pressed into the clay, with no border.
entries.means: Made by Josiah Wedgwood & Sons. From 1860 to 1930 the three-character date code is impressed beside or below it. '& CO' or the spelling WEDGEWOOD is another maker.
entries.date_note: Used long before and after the date codes; the photo is from about 1780.

sources.where: the impressed mark the code sits beside

visual.object: Platter, Wedgwood, about 1780
visual.credit: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Open Access (CC0), via Wikimedia Commons; cropped by Heirloom.

entries.name: ENGLAND, impressed with WEDGWOOD
entries.looks_like: The word ENGLAND in capitals, impressed below or near WEDGWOOD.
entries.means: Added from 1891. It usually decides between the two cycles of year letters (1860-1885 and 1886-1906); small wares and some home-market wares lack it.

visual.method: The word ENGLAND in impressed capitals, per antique-marks-wedgwood and etruria-antiques-wedgwood-marks and thepotteries-wedgwood-dating; set in Libre Caslon Text, as the punch's typeface is not recorded.
visual.credit: Drawn by Heirloom from the published descriptions; not a photograph.

entries.name: MADE IN ENGLAND, impressed with WEDGWOOD
entries.looks_like: The words MADE IN ENGLAND impressed near WEDGWOOD.
entries.means: On some wares from 1898 and generally from about 1908.

visual.method: The words MADE IN ENGLAND in impressed capitals, per W1 and Godden (1964, p. 659); set in Libre Caslon Text, as the punch's typeface is not recorded.
visual.credit: Drawn by Heirloom from the published descriptions; not a photograph.

entries.date_note: W1 and Godden (1964, p. 659): from c. 1898, mainly after about 1910.

swan with 1 (agrees with the table, not with Litchfield)

entries.means: The Worcester Royal Porcelain Co. The year code is printed below or around it from 1862 to 1963; 'Royal Worcester England' is added round it from 1891.
entries.date_note: Burton and Hobson give this mark 1851-62 and 'under a crown 1862 onwards'.

visual.method: The letter W with 3 dots, added one a year on alternate sides starting on the right, as Sandon (1973, pp. 246-248) prints them ('W.' for 1951, '.W.' for 1952) and Godden (1964, pp. 698-699) counts them; each new dot is drawn further out. The year sign alone, in its W form.
visual.credit: Drawn by Heirloom from the published descriptions; not a photograph.

entries.date_note: R1 lists years only to 1956 (W or R-in-circle with 6 dots) and says the series continued into the 1960s with dots round the R in a circle. R2 and R4 list W plus dots to 13 dots = 1963. R2 notes the use was inconsistent and many pieces of this period are undated.

Smithsonian Open Access API (Cooper Hewitt records): marks described in words, front views only, 2026-11-22

Internet Archive, pre-1929 books: Chaffers, Marks and Monograms (1912); Litchfield, Pottery and Porcelain (1912 and 1925); Burton and Hobson, Handbook of Marks (1909); Barber, Marks of American Potters (1904)

Public-domain books pass, 2026-11-22: Barber, Pottery and Porcelain of the United States (1893, 1901) p. 409 and Marks of American Potters (1904) p. 120 print only the 0-, 1- and 14-flame marks; the later marks post-date 1929.

Open-collections photo pass, 2026-11-24: Cleveland Museum of Art open-access API (CC0; marks read on its 3400 px base views), Art Institute of Chicago API (CC0 items; serves only 843 px, no legible mark of this year), Rijksmuseum data API (one front view per item), SMK API (no matching ceramics), Minneapolis Institute of Art search (one view per item), Europeana open-reuse search (no item photographs of these marks). Finna.fi showed a bot check and was not searched; DigitaltMuseum needs an API key.
Not drawn: the sources give the system, not the mark's layout (and only one source describes it).
visual.note: No licence-barred image was found; the gap is that no open photo or public-domain facsimile of this mark turned up.
